title: AddTenantCostRollup migration fails on TimescaleDB ≥2.18 — RLS after columnstore enable is rejected; blocks every deploy
evidence: log: aqua-db-migrate ... migration: AddTenantCostRollup1805000000000, error: operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 reframes `timescaledb.compress` as columnstore mode on the hypertable; once columnstore is on, the engine rejects subsequent vanilla `ALTER TABLE ENABLE/FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. Migrations that touch hypertable RLS must run RLS *before* the compression configuration, not after.
notes: Symptom: db-migrate container exits with `Migration failed ... operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` BEFORE any service container starts; entire deploy chain blocks at this single migration. Architectural fix (T1, reorder operations to honour columnstore lock-out): up() now runs CREATE TABLE → CREATE INDEX → RLS (ENABLE/FORCE/CREATE POLICY) → create_hypertable → SET (timescaledb.compress, ...) → add_compression_policy → add_retention_policy. down() reordered to remove TimescaleDB policies first, then DROP TABLE CASCADE — avoids the columnstore-vs-ALTER restriction entirely (no intermediate ALTER TABLE / DROP POLICY needed; CASCADE tears down policies, RLS state, indexes, hypertable metadata, columnstore chunks in one shot). Sensor-service migration (sensor-service/src/database/migrations/1735900000000-CreateSensorMetrics.ts) audited and is unaffected — it has compression but no RLS, so no ordering conflict.

title: AddTenantCostRollup migration — TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces RLS ⊥ columnstore mutual exclusion; reorder alone insufficient
evidence: log: error: "columnstore cannot be used on table with row security"
rule_violated: TimescaleDB ≥2.18 enforces a HARD MUTUAL EXCLUSION between RLS and columnstore on the same hypertable. The RLS-first reorder under INFRA-CRITICAL-006 traded `operation not supported on hypertables that have columnstore enabled` (compression-then-RLS) for `columnstore cannot be used on table with row security` (RLS-then-compression). Engine refuses both sequences — order does not unlock either side.
notes:
Architectural fork (must pick ONE):
  (A) keep columnstore, drop RLS — moves tenant isolation enforcement entirely to the service layer.
  (B) keep RLS, drop columnstore — preserves DB-level defense-in-depth, loses ~50% storage savings on cold buckets.

Decision: (B). User-confirmed (response: 'b'). Rationale:
- Multi-tenant SaaS — tenant isolation is the load-bearing invariant; RLS is the DB-level guard.
- Table scale at documented retention: ~29k rows/day × 90 days = ~2.6M rows total; PostgreSQL handles this trivially.
- Compression savings (~1-2 GB/year) are immaterial vs the integrity guarantee.
- Future cold-storage compression can be reintroduced via a continuous aggregate (no RLS on the aggregate, RLS-equivalent filter pushed into the materialized query) when the dataset grows enough to justify it.

Fix landed:
- Removed `ALTER TABLE … SET (timescaledb.compress, …)` block.
- Removed `add_compression_policy(…, INTERVAL '14 days', …)` call.

title: Boot signal `migration_runner_applied` never fires after db-migrate centralization — pattern only matched cold-start hot path
evidence: Deploy log run 24636862240 (boot signal assertion: 23 signal(s) pending across 12 services for 12+ rounds, all healthy)
rule_violated: WS7 / ADR-016 Phase F deploy gate: every service in required-signals.yaml MUST emit each declared signal within its window. After db-migrate centralization, every service's migration runner sees 0 pending migrations on warm start and logs `No pending migrations on "<schema>"` — that text does NOT contain the substring `migration(s)` (with parens), so the signal never matches and the deploy gate rejects every deploy even though all containers are healthy and migrations have been applied centrally.
notes:
Architectural fix (T1, single canonical signal source):

1. MigrationRunnerService.onApplicationBootstrap() now emits a canonical end-of-run log line — `Migration runner complete for schema "<sourceSchema>": tenants=<N>` — at the success exit. Fires unconditionally on both cold-start (>0 pending applied) and warm-start (0 pending) paths. Failure paths (security throw, runner exception) intentionally do NOT emit it, so the contract still proves the runner reached the success exit (no false positive).
2. required-signals.yaml signal_library.migration_runner_applied pattern updated from `"migration(s)"` (substring of "Applied N migration(s): …") to `"Migration runner complete"` (substring of the new canonical line).
3. The pre-existing per-schema logs (`Applied N migration(s) on "X"` and `No pending migrations on "X"`) are unchanged — they still document per-schema progress; they're just no longer the contract surface for the deploy gate.
4. Refactored the orphan `if (!tenantAware) return;` early-return into a single tenantAware branch so the canonical complete log lands once per runner invocation regardless of fan-out shape.

Why not change the signal pattern alone: a looser substring like `"migration"` would match `migration failed`, `running migration`, etc. — any noise word that happens to mention migrations would falsely satisfy the contract. The canonical-log approach pins the signal to a single emission point in the code, which is the discipline required by required-signals.yaml's signalSource convention.

title: DEFECT-3: messaging E2E test harness lacked withTenantContext helper — direct dataSource.* calls in tests bypass the middleware-set ALS, causing TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION on every direct write
evidence: GitHub Actions runs 24659776761 / 24660420932 / 24659561676 — every messaging E2E run shows hundreds of `TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION: Direct write to source schema messaging.channels blocked`

Tenant routing is ALS-driven: requestContextStorage carries `schemaName = tenant_<uuid>`, the patched pg pool reads it on every checkout and pins search_path. Direct dataSource.* calls in tests run OUTSIDE any request → ALS empty → pool falls back to source schema → trigger fires.

apps/messaging-service/test/e2e-setup.ts (PRE-FIX): no helper to wrap direct DB calls in a synthetic ALS frame; tests had no clean way to perform fixture writes / OUTBOX inspection without tripping the source-schema write guard.

The production middleware chain establishes that frame for HTTP requests; tests doing direct DB calls need an explicit helper.
notes: Architectural fix (T1, parity-by-construction): added `withTenantContext(tenantId, fn)` helper to apps/messaging-service/test/e2e-setup.ts. Imports `requestContextStorage` from backend-common (the singleton ALS instance the production middleware + TenantConnectionBootstrap pool patch use), composes parent store + new store with `tenantId` + `schemaName = tenant_<uuid>`, runs `fn` inside the synthetic frame. Direct test-side dataSource calls now route to the tenant schema just like production GraphQL writes. Invariant tests/invariants/messaging-e2e-tenant-context.spec.ts asserts the helper exists, imports the right ALS instance, and composes the parent store (catches future regressions that would silently break tenant routing in tests). NOTE: this commit lands the helper; the residual `TENANT_ISOLATION_VIOLATION` errors observed in the GraphQL request flow on the same E2E runs have a separate root cause (ALS frame not propagating across some async boundary inside the NestJS CQRS / Apollo handler chain) and require a separate diagnostic + fix — tracked as the next finding.

title: rumqttc 0.25.1 transitively pulls vulnerable rustls-webpki 0.102.8 (RUSTSEC-2026-0098 + 0099)

title: farm.farm_outbox missing 5 modern OutboxEntityBase columns (tenantId, aggregateId, nextAttemptAt, idempotencyKey, isDeadLettered) — blocks SchemaDriftValidator boot signal

title: Faz 2 D-2 partial — mlock pin process pages in RAM via mlockall(MCL_CURRENT|MCL_FUTURE) (memfd_secret + panic_zeroize registry land in #310 + #311)

An attacker with post-reboot forensic access to the swap partition (eMMC dump, cloud-VM hypervisor escape) could extract the master key from a paged-out copy even though the in-RAM copy was correctly drop-zeroized. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::mlock submodule wrapping mlockall(MCL_CURRENT | MCL_FUTURE) — locks every current page AND every future allocation including async stack frames + heap regrowth. Idempotent (kernel ignores second call), structured error taxonomy (NotPermitted/InsufficientLimit/TemporaryFailure/UnknownErrno/UnsupportedPlatform) discriminating the EPERM/ENOMEM/EAGAIN/other errno classes, MlockState{locked_current, locked_future} return shape captures the actual posture for audit emission, proc_self_vm_locked_bytes() audit accessor parses /proc/self/status VmLck for runtime verification + future observability metrics. Wired into harden_process() boot sequence BEFORE panic-hook install (idempotent ordering — both calls are commutative). Best-effort by default (mlock requires CAP_IPC_LOCK or sufficient RLIMIT_MEMLOCK; container envs often lack this); structured warn log with operator-readable diagnostic when mlockall fails, future config.security.mlock_enforce flag will fail-close boot. Architectural property: complements existing zeroize-on-drop layer at the keystore::secret module — secrets are scrubbed when the value drops AND no copy of the page reaches swap while the value is alive. Choosing mlockall over selective mlock is intentional: secret bytes can transiently appear on async stack frames between awaits which are not addressable from the secret's owner, AND Rust's allocator may freely move heap allocations across pages requiring re-mlock per realloc. Pinning the entire address space is the only architecturally honest answer for a Rust-async process; memory cost on RPi CM4 (1-8 GB RAM) is acceptable since the agent's working set is ~150-300 MB at p99.

title: Faz 2 D-2 partial — memfd_secret(2) primitive (Linux 5.14+) MemfdSecretRegion strongest in-process secret container (panic_zeroize lands in #311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening — memfd_secret slice. Pre-Batch-#310 the in-process defense layers were: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B, kernel-level coredump suppression), mlockall (Batch #309 Layer C, pages off swap), panic-abort hook (Layer D, no destructor unwinding on panic), zeroize-on-drop (Layer E, scrub at value drop). Critical gap: NONE of those prevent (a) /proc/<pid>/mem reads from a privileged process post-compromise, (b) hibernation image inclusion via swsusp, (c) live-migration / VM snapshot inclusion via KVM. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::memfd_secret submodule wrapping the Linux 5.14+ memfd_secret(2) syscall. Pages allocated through MemfdSecretRegion are excluded from ALL of: kernel direct-map (the kernel itself cannot reach them outside the owning process via set_direct_map_invalid_noflush()), /proc/<pid>/mem (kernel rejects reads on memfd_secret VMAs), hibernation images (swsusp skips), KVM guest RAM dumps (host hypervisor cannot snapshot). MemfdSecretRegion owns (fd, ptr, len) tuple with manual unsafe Send (no aliasing — exclusive ownership), NOT Sync (matches Vec<u8>'s exclusivity model — &mut self required for write access; callers needing shared access wrap in Mutex). Drop impl munmaps + closes; kernel automatically zeroes pages on release. Constructor allocate(len) rejects len==0 with structured ZeroLength variant; runtime probe is_supported() returns bool (one syscall + close, ENOSYS detection). Fallback path: when kernel < 5.14 or built without CONFIG_SECRETMEM, allocate() returns Err(NotSupported); caller falls back to mlock + anonymous-mmap path (Batch #309). Architectural property pinned: 'secrets in memfd_secret OR mlock-pinned' is the contract; the caller picks the strongest available. title: Faz 2 D-2 closure — panic_zeroize registry walks registered secret regions zeroing each BEFORE std::process::abort() (closes ULTRA-HIGH-016 D-2 arc with #309+#310+#311)
rule_violated: Plan §5 Faz 2 D-2 + ADR-018 §7 + ADR-019 §5 in-process hardening — panic_zeroize slice + arc closure. Pre-Batch-#311 the in-process defense layer cake was: prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) (Layer B), mlockall (Batch #309 Layer C), memfd_secret (Batch #310 Layer C+, when supported), zeroize-on-drop (Layer E), panic-abort hook (Layer D). CRITICAL GAP: between the panic instant and the kernel-reap, secret pages are still mapped + readable by a concurrent thread / by the kernel itself reading process memory. On a panicking multi-threaded program the panic hook runs on ONE thread; OTHER threads continue running until abort() actually fires. That window is small but architecturally non-zero. Architectural fix: new process_hardening::panic_zeroize submodule providing a global registry of (NonNull<u8>, usize) secret regions with register/unregister/scrub-all surface. The panic-abort hook now walks the registry zeroing each region BEFORE std::process::abort(), shrinking the window to 'during the zeroize loop'. Best-effort with try_lock + 100ms deadline so a panic mid-register/unregister does not deadlock the hook (in that rare case the kernel still releases pages on process exit + the mlock + zeroize-on-drop layers remain in effect — defense-in-depth optimization, not primary guarantee). OnceLock + Mutex<Vec<RegisteredRegion>> shape: lazy init keeps no-secret-allocation programs zero-cost; Mutex serializes register/unregister/scrub access; poison-recovery via into_inner() means a previous lock-holder's panic doesn't break registration for survivors. Raw pointers (NonNull<u8>) chosen over references because the registry is 'static + the secret regions have shorter lifetimes that no single 'a satisfies; caller register/unregister pairing is the documented contract. Manual unsafe Send on RegisteredRegion: pointer + length values are integers; moving the slot is safe under the caller's region-validity contract. test_only_clear() crate-private accessor lets test fixtures reset between cases without exposing a production reset API. title: shared.audit_logs + admin.audit_logs have NO retention policy registered with the canonical RetentionEnforcementService
rule_violated: Every regulated audit-log table MUST have a retention policy registered with the canonical RetentionEnforcementService — uncontrolled growth is an integrity risk + compliance flag (storage exhaustion, query slowdown, no documented disposal cycle)
notes: observability-service registers 4 policies for its own tables. shared.audit_logs (cross-service canonical audit) + admin.audit_logs (SUPER_ADMIN cross-tenant audit) are owned by admin-api but have NO retention policy registration anywhere — rows accumulate forever. Cure: AdminApiRetentionBootstrapModule registers both policies via registerRetentionPolicy with retentionDays=7*365 (SOC 2 CC4 floor) + legalHoldClause="NOT \"legalHold\"" so held rows are excluded from cleanup, mirroring the auth/farm cleanup-cron filter. The canonical RetentionEnforcementService cron runs daily at 03:00 UTC; per-policy try/catch ensures one failure doesn't stall the others.

title: 20 createBaseEvent emits have no canonical interface — producer can drift payload shape without consumer compile break
rule_violated: Every createBaseEvent('<EventType>', ...) call site MUST have a matching <EventType>Event interface in libs/event-contracts/src/ — without it a producer-side field bump goes silent at the consumer, inviting the same regression class as SubscriptionPastDue
notes: Discovered during W0.E (event-contract type integrity) work; allowlisted at the time as ORPHAN-EVENT-CONTRACT-001..018 in tests/invariants/event-contract-emit-has-interface.spec.ts pending domain audit. Cure shipped here: 16 messaging interfaces (channel lifecycle ×5, message lifecycle ×7, compliance ×2, operational ×2) + 4 automation interfaces (sensor-service program/tag events). Each enters its domain union (MessagingEvent | AutomationEvent), and AnyPlatformEvent absorbs AutomationEvent so the platform-wide type still covers everything. Allowlist drained to empty.

title: registry-integrity invariant + adoption-invariant carry pre-existing legacy drift — three-store + adoption-invariants suites failing on main
rule_violated: Pre-existing CI invariant suites must be green on main before any new work lands; legacy drift in registry cross-store traceability and adoption SSoT classification creates noise that masks real regressions
notes: Discovered while validating W0 closures. Three-store-invariants had 4 entries failing the closing_commits / Closes-trailer / review-file-anchor checks (PROC-MEDIUM-005, ORPHAN-HIGH-014, INFRA-MEDIUM-014, plus 35+ more found by comprehensive scan). title: ai-service Anthropic call NOT wrapped in canonical CircuitBreaker — runaway cost + cascading-failure risk
rule_violated: Every external API call MUST be wrapped in the canonical CircuitBreakerService.execute() — without it a degraded upstream cascades into request queues, ties up DB connections, and (for billable APIs) accumulates uncapped per-tenant cost
notes: Cure: AgentModule imports CircuitBreakerModule (canonical from W0.B); AgentRunnerService injects CircuitBreakerService; the anthropic.messages.create call at line 195 wrapped via execute() with serviceName='anthropic-api', tenantId from request, failureMode='fail-closed' (billable boundary — degraded service must NOT fall back to a free response). Per-tenant tenantKey isolates noisy-neighbor: one tenant's runaway agent loop cannot trip the breaker for everyone.

title: 5 schema-owning services lack TypeORM CLI data-source.ts — operator tooling cannot run migration:show / migration:revert
rule_violated: Every schema-owning service MUST ship a TypeORM CLI data-source.ts at src/database/data-source.ts so operator tooling (`npm run typeorm -- migration:show / migration:revert`) can read schema state and roll back migrations independent of the long-running service
notes: Cure: each missing service gets a data-source.ts following the canonical pattern from apps/alert-engine/src/database/data-source.ts. Migrations glob points at the actual on-disk location (src/migrations vs src/database/migrations) per-service. migrationsRun:false (the runner service inside the long-running app owns execution); the CLI data-source is for operator-only paths.

title: Two divergent SENSITIVE_KEYS lists — audit interceptor + structured logger redact different sets, leaks possible at one path that the other catches
rule_violated: PII / secret redaction key sets MUST be a single source of truth across every redaction site; divergence between sites means a key redacted in one path leaks through the other (e.g., 'access_token' redacted in logs but written verbatim to audit metadata)
notes: Audit-side Set: {password, token, secret, accesstoken, refreshtoken, authorization, creditcard, ssn, cvv, pin, apikey, privatekey}. Logger regex: {password, passwd, secret, token, authorization, apikey, api_key, access_token, refresh_token, private_key, credentials?}. Each catches what the other misses. Cure: single SSoT exported as both Set (for hash-set comparison in audit) and RegExp (for fast match in logger), driven by one master array. Underscore variants + abbreviations covered uniformly.

title: Stripe webhook idempotency uses Redis-only dedup — Redis restart or eviction allows duplicate billing-event processing
rule_violated: Webhook idempotency for billable financial events MUST be persistent — Redis-only dedup is volatile (lost on restart, evicted under memory pressure, missing on cold cache). A replayed Stripe webhook for the same event_id MUST be processed exactly once across the system lifetime, not the Redis instance lifetime
notes: Cure: persistent DB table billing.stripe_webhook_events with UNIQUE constraint on (event_id) — INSERT-on-receive becomes the dedup primitive (constraint violation = duplicate, no further processing). Redis layer kept as a fast-path cache (avoids hitting DB on every replay), but the DB row is the authoritative source. event_id PK in Stripe is guaranteed unique across all events. Schema: event_id varchar(255) PK, event_type varchar(64), received_at timestamptz, processed_at timestamptz nullable (set on success), outcome varchar(32). Same shape pattern as outbox event-id table.

title: Stripe webhook payment.failureReason persists raw failureMessage with PII (card last-4, billing details) past audit retention window
rule_violated: PII originating from upstream APIs MUST be masked before storage in operational tables — operational rows have indefinite retention (until tenant erasure) while audit rows have a bounded compliance window. Persisting raw 'card ending in 4242 declined' strings in payments.failureReason leaks PII into long-term storage where the audit-side immutable copy already preserves the regulatory record
notes: Cure: maskPii() the failureMessage substring before constructing failureReason that lands in Payment.failureReason and PaymentFailedEvent.failureReason. The maskPii utility (libs/backend-common/src/utils/pii-mask.util.ts) already redacts credit card, SSN, email, phone, and IPv4 patterns. Audit-log row keeps the raw form via separate path (immutable + 7y retention; tenant erasure clears with the rest).

title: auth-service GDPR erasure path bypasses canonical legal-hold registry — held-tenant user erasure proceeds unconditionally
rule_violated: Every destructive operation against tenant data MUST consult the canonical legal-hold registry before proceeding. GDPR right-to-erasure is a destructive op with PII-anonymisation finality; running it on a tenant under litigation hold destroys evidence the legal team is duty-bound to preserve
notes: Cure: GdprComplianceService constructor injects LegalHoldService (canonical from W0.C); executeErasure() calls legalHoldService.assertNoHold(tenantId, 'tenant') before the anonymise transaction. Throws LegalHoldActiveError if blocked — operator gets a clear error, runbook explains how to obtain a release before re-trying. The hold check is inside the transaction wrapper so a hold applied AFTER the check but before the UPDATE is also blocked at the DB-trigger layer (BEFORE DELETE on legalHold-flagged audit rows).

title: admin-api tenant deprovisioning bypasses legal-hold registry — held-tenant DROP SCHEMA proceeds unconditionally
rule_violated: Every destructive operation against tenant data MUST consult the canonical legal-hold registry before proceeding. Tenant deprovisioning issues DROP SCHEMA on the tenant's per-tenant schema (irreversible at the DB level); running this on a tenant under litigation hold destroys evidence the legal team is duty-bound to preserve
notes: Cure: TenantProvisioningService constructor injects LegalHoldService (canonical from W0.C); deprovisionTenant() calls assertNoHold(tenantId, 'tenant') as the FIRST validation step (before backup, before resource removal, before cleanupTenantSchema). Throws LegalHoldActiveError if blocked. Mirrors LEGAL-HIGH-005 cure for the auth-side erasure path.

title: auth-service ScheduleModule never registered — @Cron decorator on audit-log retention cleanup is silent dead code
rule_violated: Every @Cron-decorated method MUST be hosted by a service whose module imports ScheduleModule (forRoot or forFeature) somewhere in its module tree. Without this, the NestJS scheduler never registers the cron job and the method body is dead code — silent operational failure, not a build error
notes: Discovered while validating AUDITTRAIL-HIGH-001 (audit retention 90d→7y). The 7-year retention floor relies on @Cron scheduledLogCleanup running daily at 02:00 UTC; without ScheduleModule registered, the cron NEVER fires and auth.audit_logs grows indefinitely. AUDITTRAIL-HIGH-001 cure was therefore latent — the floor was set in code but never enforced at runtime. Cure: register ScheduleModule.forRoot() in auth-service AppModule. Companion check: invariant test that asserts every service with @Cron decorators has ScheduleModule in its imports tree (catches future regressions of the same class).
